- automated fallback behavior (how quickly, to what version)
- pinning rules during the trial window
- telemetry gates and exact thresholds that trigger rollback

Can you send something formal we can attach to the internal change request? Also, are there any expected maintenance windows or elevated risk periods?

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Elaine — thanks for flagging. High-level response below; attaching a concise proposal (stability-sentinel-proposal.pdf) you can drop into your change request.

Short answer: yes — we can commit to an explicit automated fallback and version-hold during the trial window and document gates that will trigger rollback. Key points in the attached:

- Canary cadence: 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 24 hours (with manual hold at each step).
- Automated fallback: if p99 latency increases by > 40% vs baseline for two consecutive 10-min windows OR error rate > 1.5% for three consecutive 5-min windows, traffic auto-routes to the pinned stable version. Failover target will be the prior GA model version (we keep a rolling preserve of last 3 GA builds).
- Pinning: a hard pin can be applied to the account-level routing rule for the trial duration (do not auto-unpin).
- Communication: automated high-priority alert to Novacorp ops + Redwood on-call within 2 minutes of trigger; follow-up post-mortem within 48 hours for any auto-fallback event.
- SLA carveout: we propose a short, scoped exception for the 24-hour ramping window allowing a single auto-fallback attempt without crediting, provided the fallback succeeds; any customer-facing downtime beyond that is subject to normal SLA terms.

I’ve looped in David for commercial language and Aditya for the exact telemetry thresholds and the automatic-fallback implementation notes. If that looks good I’ll prepare the sign-off doc you can attach.

Best,
Laura

Elaine / team — technical detail from the runtime side and proposed conservative defaults you can rely on. I kept this brief so legal/ops can consume easily. See attached telemetry CSV for exact numbers.

Implementation summary:
- Baseline capture: we compute a 7-day p99 and error baseline per endpoint and region. For the canary we compare a rolling 10-minute window to that baseline.
- Rollback triggers (automatic):
  * p99_canary > p99_baseline * 1.40 for two consecutive 10-min windows -> trigger autofallback to pinned_version (previous GA).
  * error_rate_canary > 1.5% for three consecutive 5-min windows -> trigger autofallback.
  * sudden traffic surge causing queue depth > 1000 (region) -> trigger immediate traffic quiesce and alert; auto-fallback if not resolved within 5 minutes.
- Pin semantics: pinning sets a TTL-less routing override at the account level; only a user with "routing_admin" rights in Novacorp or Redwood engineering can unpin. We will not auto-clear the pin.
- Autofallback mechanics: we perform a weighted reroute over 60 seconds to move traffic back to the pinned version; if at 30 minutes the prior version has not stabilized (p99 within 20% of baseline), we hold traffic and escalate to on-call to avoid flip-flopping.
- Telemetry/alerts: PagerDuty high priority + Slack #novacorp-incidents + webhook to Novacorp ops.

Operational asks for Novacorp: please confirm who is allowed to authorize unpin (list of emails) and whether you want the 30-minute recovery bound David suggested.

-Aditya
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
aditya_rao@redwood.com
(Attachment: telemetry-thresholds.csv)
